features.name: Scan resume after interruption
features.desc:
When a full scan is interrupted mid-process (app killed, crash), resume from work already completed rather than restarting from the beginning.

BUILT AND VERIFIED 2026-07-29. Implemented via per-folder completion records rather than the linear cursor this record originally specified -- folder_stats already records exactly 'this folder was fully processed with N files and B bytes', which is a better cursor than a last-completed-path because it handles partial folders and does not care about processing order. v16 migration adds scanSessionId to folder_stats and currentScanSessionId to library_sources: without a run identifier, folder_stats rows from a killed scan are indistinguishable from rows left by a previous completed scan, so resuming would skip folders the interrupted run never touched (harmless on a first-ever import, silently wrong on any re-import).

Also fixed a prerequisite bug found while building this: the launch-time 'scanning' -> 'error' reset that sorriva-context.html documents was never actually built. checkForChanges' guard skipped any source stuck at 'scanning' outright, so a hard-terminated scan produced no alert, no resume, and a source showing a live ScanStatusPanel forever. Now treats 'scanning' with no active task in this process as a killed scan.

Alert offers Resume / Start Over / Cancel. Session id is written before the scan starts (survives termination), left in place on error (resume needs it), cleared on genuine completion and by confirmAndScanSource (so an explicit rescan can never inherit a stale session and skip folders).

VERIFIED: killed mid-scan, resumed, skipped 31 files in 4 already-complete folders, 642 remaining, progress reported against the filtered total. Negative test also passed -- a subsequent manual scan rescanned all 673 files with no skip lines.

NOTE: artwork passes are NOT yet resumable -- see HANDOFF-scanner-architecture-2026-07-29.md item 5. Quitting during the artwork phase still loses that work, because nothing except a scan ever starts those passes.

features.name: Overlapping share detection
features.desc: When two library sources share an overlapping folder path (e.g. /Music II and /Music II/Pat Metheny Group), scanning the subfolder share will find files already indexed by the parent share under a different sourceId. The subfolder scan produces 0 tracks in its report because the album record belongs to the parent sourceId. Detect this condition at scan start by checking if any existing source covers the same folder path, and surface a warning rather than silently producing an empty scan. Deduplication key is folderPath — same folder always resolves to the same album record.

features.name: Manual Artwork Override
features.desc: Context menu on albums allows user to set custom artwork from photo library or camera, or delete existing art. Setting artwork writes artManualOverride=true, blocking all automated passes. Deleting artwork resets artManualOverride=false and clears artPathFull/artPathThumb, re-enabling all automated passes on next foreground.

features.name: Album Split Edge Cases
features.desc: Superseded by the 2026-07-25 fix that removed resolveAlbum's title+artist fallback. That fallback was causing wrong MERGES — compilation folders sharing an ALBUM tag collapsed into one album via the shared 'Various Artists' artist row. folderPath is now the sole album deduplication key; one folder is one album. What this record originally called 'splitting' (e.g. multi-disc siblings, same album stored in separate folders) is the accepted, intended behavior of that design, not a defect. Closed rather than reworked — reopening the old title+artist fallback to 'fix' folder-based splits would reintroduce the merge bug this record predates. See sorriva-scanner-handoff-2026-07-25.md §1.3 and §8.

features.name: Scanner identity integrity — test seam + WP-02 completion
features.desc: Blocking, constitutional (I-009 no silent critical failures). SMBScanner mints a new UUID for Track.id on every scan and calls the non-idempotent upsertTrack, so rescanning an existing library silently fails to update rows or risks orphaning legacy_track_map — nothing surfaces the failure. ScannerTests cannot catch this: it never instantiates SMBScanner, only a hand-written test double (bScannerTestSeam). Sequence per sorriva-scanner-handoff-2026-07-25.md §6: (1) build MediaSourceReader protocol seam — SMB + fixture-backed implementations, do not change the existing SMB connection pattern (200ms throttle, 64KB reads, fresh connection per file); (2) rewrite the 4 existing acceptance tests to drive the real scanner through the seam — expect 1–3 to fail, reproducing the WP-02 defect under test; (3) implement remaining WP-02 items (path normalization, upsertTrackIdempotent as the production call, folder-level GRDB transactions, thrown errors in place of try? writes, ScanReport failure counts) until tests 1–5 are green; (4) add regression tests for the 2026-07-25 artist/album fixes (tests 6–17); (5) then run diagnostics against bMissingTracksInAlbum — may already be resolved by the folder-transaction fix in step 3. Prerequisite for trusting any other scanner work, including the cosmetic-polish batch in fScannerPolish. PROGRESS 2026-07-26: step 1 (MediaSourceReader protocol seam) built and verified against the real NAS — 476 tracks, clean scan, no regression. Step 2 (rewrite acceptance tests to drive the real scanner) done for the primary reproduction: testScannerRescanUpdatesChangedTags now fails cleanly and correctly, proving the WP-02 defect under test for the first time — confirmed via direct SQLite error capture (UNIQUE constraint failed: tracks.filePath) before reverting to try?. Also required and completed an unplanned but necessary prerequisite: SorrivaDatabase.shared had no test isolation and would have written fixture data into the real device library — fixed by routing to an isolated temp-directory sqlite file when XCTestConfigurationFilePath is present. Step 3 (implement the actual fix: upsertTrackIdempotent as the production call, path normalization, folder-level transactions, thrown errors, ScanReport failure counts) not yet started — that is what turns the new red test green. Committed as v0.0.38. COMPLETE 2026-07-26: full 1-17 test list from the handoff now exists and passes as designed (v0.0.39, v0.0.40). Tests 1-2 (identity defect) were red then fixed. Tests 6-14 (artist/album regression) all pass, and caught a real, previously-unknown fillFromPath bug along the way (single-folder-depth case missing the same albumArtist guard the default case had) — fixed same session. Tests 15, 17 pass as regression guards. Test 16 correctly documents a known, deferred limitation (large PICTURE block preceding VORBIS_COMMENT within the 64KB header read window) — tracked under fScanFailureUtility, not fixed here by design. Test 3 (legacy_track_map preservation) and tests 4/5 (folder-transaction rollback) as originally envisioned were superseded by a smaller, safer design: per-file write retry + fallback into the existing scan_skips mechanism, after Tom correctly challenged why a single bad write should lose an entire folder instead of just that one file. clearLocalLibrary() now also clears scan_skips. Two new roadmap items opened from this work: bScanConnectionExhaustionOnRepeatedScans (real, observed, not yet investigated) and fScannerDatabaseInjection (future, not urgent).

Not blocking and should not be scheduled ahead of fScannerIdentityIntegrity, since none of these are verifiable by test until the scanner test seam exists. features.name: Albums indexed with fewer tracks than the folder contains
features.desc:
Some albums appear in the library with only one track while the corresponding NAS folder holds a full album. Root cause not yet identified — needs testing before a fix is proposed. Ruled out by code inspection: file enumeration in collectAudioFiles is recursive, lowercases extensions and correctly skips dotfiles; read failures do not cause missing rows because a Track is still written from path data when a header read fails; and the albumCache folderKey is checked first so every file in a folder always resolves to the same album. Remaining candidates, in order of likelihood: (1) an interrupted incremental scan — deleteTracksInFolder removes every track in a changed folder before re-adding them one at a time, so cancellation or backgrounding partway leaves the folder partially populated, and fScanResume is not built yet so nothing repairs it; (2) SMBClient listDirectory returning a truncated entry set on large folders, consistent with known UNAS Pro session behaviour; (3) a full scan cancelled mid-folder. Diagnostics to run next session, cheapest first: pick one affected album, count the files in that folder on the NAS, then grep the scan log for the 'SCAN: folder done' line on that path and compare its reported count; check filesFound on the 'SCAN: START' line against the true library total; query scan_skips for that folder to confirm skips are not involved. UPDATE 2026-07-28 (gate-readiness audit): a real, newly-discovered interaction with bFailedReadCreatesWrongAlbumFromFallback (fixed same session). This record's own 'ruled out' reasoning explicitly relied on 'a Track is still written from path data when a header read fails' -- that exact behavior was removed by the fallback fix, for good reason (it was causing wrong album names). Side effect, not previously considered: a track that now fails BOTH its initial read AND all 5 retry attempts has ZERO representation in the library, where before it would have had at least a path-derived stub row. This may be making this bug worse for that specific case. Not yet confirmed either way -- needs checking as part of whatever session investigates this next, using the diagnostics already specified below.

UPDATE 2026-07-29: lowered to Low priority per Tom. Did not manifest in a full clean 673-file scan after the connection-exhaustion fix -- 663 tracks plus 10 skips all resolved on retry attempt 1 accounted for every file. Plausibly a symptom of connection exhaustion rather than an independent bug: reads failed, and the retry scheduler that should have recovered them was itself burning connections in an exhausted state. Keeping open at Low pending several more scans before calling it. Note the diagnostic this record recommends (comparing the 'SCAN: folder done' count against real files in the folder) was INVALID until 2026-07-29 -- that line reported the enumerated file count, not persisted tracks, so a folder where every read failed still logged its full track count. Now fixed to report written vs enumerated with an explicit shortfall. CLOSED 2026-08-03 (doc-vs-code audit, zero build effort): the silent-drop mechanism is structurally closed - resolveAlbum keys on folderPath alone (no tag-derived merge or split), a failed read records a ledger skip instead of a path-derived stub, upsertTrackIdempotent removed the rescan write-loss vector, and the ledger accounts for every planned file so any regression surfaces as UNACCOUNTED greater than zero. What remains is visible degraded completeness under NAS failure, which is accounted and surfaced, not a silent drop. Reopen as a NEW defect if a genuine missing-track case recurs.

features.name: No warning for duplicate albums present on disk
features.desc: Library contains parent folders holding two parallel sets of the same discs — for example 12 Inch 80s - Pop (CD1) alongside 12 Inch 80s - Pop [Disc 1]. This is a data condition on the NAS, not something the scanner produces, and Sorriva should not attempt to resolve it automatically: choosing which copy survives is a destructive user decision. Scope is a post-scan report that warns the user which albums appear to be genuine duplicates, never automatic action. Detection should use the MD5 of the decoded audio stream carried in the FLAC STREAMINFO block, which already sits inside the first 42 bytes of every file and is therefore captured for free during the existing 64KB tag read — one new column, no additional I/O. Matching on audio MD5 ignores tag and filename differences entirely. Known limits: identifies copied files rather than the same CD independently ripped twice, since separate rips produce different PCM, and is FLAC-only as MP3 and M4A carry no equivalent.

features.name: Scanner acceptance tests cannot observe the code they certify
features.desc:
ScannerTests never instantiates SMBScanner — the string does not appear in the file. testFullScanTwicePreservesIDs, testMetadataChangeUpdatesExistingTrack, testDeletedFileRemovedOnFolderRescan and testFailedWriteDoesNotMarkFolderComplete all drive SorrivaDatabaseTestable, a test double that carries its own hand-written copy of upsertTrackIdempotent annotated as the WP-02 fix. The tests therefore validate a reimplementation of the algorithm rather than the production scan path, and pass regardless of what SMBScanner actually calls. This is how WP-02 was logged complete on 2026-07-23 while the scanner still called the non-idempotent upsertTrack. Fix requires a source seam on SMBScanner so it can run against local fixture files without a live NAS — extract the SMB read and directory-walk operations behind a protocol, supply a fixture-backed implementation in tests, and rewrite the four acceptance tests to drive the real scanner through it. Until that seam exists the only honest verification of scan idempotency is manual: scan twice against the NAS and compare row counts and Track.id values. The seam is a prerequisite for verifying WP-02 and is not in WP-02's task list as written. UPDATE 2026-07-28 (gate-readiness audit): precisely scoped rather than left as a blanket concern. All 16 tests in ScannerTests.swift checked individually. 10 cover unrelated components (playback coordinator, keychain, DB migration, app environment, source resolver) where the fake database is a harmless convenience, not a risk. 2 more (testFullScanTwicePreservesIDs, testMetadataChangeUpdatesExistingTrack) genuinely overlap with newer tests built under fScannerIdentityIntegrity that DO exercise the real scanner via MediaSourceReader -- those specific behaviors are independently verified elsewhere despite this file's own version being untrustworthy on its own. That leaves exactly 2 tests with real, unverified exposure: testDeletedFileRemovedOnFolderRescan and testFailedWriteDoesNotMarkFolderComplete -- genuine scanner behaviors with no real-path equivalent found anywhere else. Recommended resolution: port these 2 specifically to the MediaSourceReader-based seam rather than reworking the whole file.

ADDRESSED 2026-08-01 by fScanLedgerUnitTests. FixtureMediaSourceReader gained beforeRead/beforeList hooks plus call counters, and the new ScanLedgerTests run the REAL SMBScanner against real synthesized FLAC files through SorrivaDatabase.shared — no reimplementation. That is the distinction this record was about: the two tests it names assert against their own copy of the logic and would pass whether or not production works.

Those two original tests have NOT yet been ported onto the seam; the new suite covers the ledger rather than replacing them. Worth doing, but the seam and the pattern now exist.

features.name: Artwork selection takes first acceptable image, not best available
features.desc: Three artwork passes run in fixed order — folder, online fetch, embedded — and the last to run wins unconditionally. Two defects result. First, the folder pass accepts the first candidate that clears the 200px floor rather than comparing all candidates in the folder: one album accepted AlbumArt_*.jpg at 450x450 without ever examining Folder.jpg in the same folder, while another reached 1000x882 only because Folder.jpg happened to sort first, and a third landed on 720x634 by accident after a timeout eliminated its first choice. Second, albumsNeedingEmbeddedArtScan filters only on embeddedArtScanned == false, so the embedded pass runs against every album including those that already have artwork, and it applies no dimension check or logging of any kind. Observed consequence: three albums whose folder pass found 1000x882 Folder.jpg were overwritten by the embedded pass with art of unknown size, and an album whose art came from online fetch was likewise overwritten. The embedded-is-always-better assumption was intentional and is usually correct for this library, since most rejected folder images were WMP-generated 200x200 Folder.jpg thumbnails, but it is currently unverifiable because embedded saves log no dimensions. Proposed solution: select by highest pixel area across all candidates from all three sources, treating format as irrelevant since dimensions are already extracted. Use pixel area rather than width, because the library contains 450x292 and 450x398 images alongside 450x450. Measure candidates by reading image headers only — PNG IHDR carries width and height at bytes 16 through 24 so 33 bytes suffices, and JPEG SOF0/SOF2 markers are almost always within the first 2KB — then perform one full read for the winner. This is cheaper than current behaviour on folders where the first candidate is rejected and a second is downloaded in full. Tie-break equal areas by filename preference: cover, then folder, then AlbumArt_*, then others. Persist the winning dimensions in two additive columns on albums so the embedded pass, which runs from a separate DB query, can compare against what the folder pass measured — this requires a v14 additive migration. Online fetch then becomes just another candidate that must beat the stored dimensions rather than a special case for albums with no art. Consequence for the 200px floor: under best-wins a 200x200 image is a legitimate winner when nothing better exists, so the floor should flag the album as low resolution rather than reject the image and leave the album blank. One open judgment: pure area selection prefers 450x450 over 450x292, which is usually right but will also discard legitimately wide cover art — decide deliberately rather than inherit it from the algorithm. SCOPING NOTE 2026-07-26: read the actual current implementation before starting (runFolderArtPass + runEmbeddedArtPass in ScanCoordinator.swift, plus an online-fetch path in ArtworkCache.swift not yet read). Confirmed the roadmap's diagnosis is accurate — folder pass fully decodes each candidate via UIImage(data:) just to check dimensions (wasteful; header-only PNG IHDR / JPEG SOF read is the fix), sorts by file SIZE in bytes as a quality proxy and takes the first candidate that clears 300px (not comparing all candidates), and albumsNeedingEmbeddedArtScan filters only on a boolean flag with no dimension comparison at all. Genuinely larger than anything else done in the 2026-07-25/26 scanner sessions — touches 2+ files, needs a v15 migration (two new dimension columns), new header-only image parsing, and redesigned album eligibility querying. Deferred to a fresh session rather than rushed. IMPORTANT CONSTRAINT for that session: the three separate passes (folder/embedded/online) must be RETAINED as separate passes — they exist to avoid concurrent NAS session pressure and per-connection timeouts, not merely as an artifact of the current (buggy) last-wins design. Best-wins selection must compare results ACROSS the passes' stored outcomes (via the new dimension columns), not collapse the passes into one combined operation. COMPLETE 2026-07-27. v15 migration, ImageDimensionReader (header-only PNG/JPEG dimension reading, verified against real generated images before writing Swift), ArtworkBestWins (pure, testable candidate selection). Embedded pass reordered first; folder pass always does a cheap header-check regardless of what embedded found, only the expensive download is conditional on winning; online fetch reverted to gap-filling-only after real testing found it overwriting correct existing artwork with wrong iTunes matches (see bArtworkArtistQuery, fArtworkManualSearchUtility). Real-world testing (not just unit tests) surfaced and fixed 3 genuine bugs in the new code before this closed: folder-pass hang on connection timeout (no reconnect — also found the download-timeout reconnect had been lost in the same rewrite), embedded pass stopping at the first track with any art instead of checking all up-to-3 and keeping the best (real case: Pat Metheny 'We Live Here' saved 200x200 over an available 1280x1280), and the online-fetch overwrite issue. 10 new tests (ArtworkSelectionTests).

features.name: Full database injection seam for SMBScanner
features.desc: SMBScanner calls SorrivaDatabase.shared directly at ~15 call sites, with no way to inject an isolated in-memory queue the way TestDatabase.makeQueue() already provides for repository/service-layer tests. 2026-07-26 solved the immediate safety problem with a smaller fix (SorrivaDatabase.shared now detects XCTestConfigurationFilePath and routes to an isolated temp-directory file per test run) — sufficient for scanner identity tests today, but not the same as real per-test isolation: it is one shared file across every test method in a run (already caused one cross-test collision during fScannerIdentityIntegrity, worked around with unique fixture paths per test), it is slower than in-memory, and it does not compose with parallel test execution. Proper fix mirrors the MediaSourceReader seam but for the database layer: thread an injectable database dependency through SMBScanner's ~15 call sites so tests can supply TestDatabase.makeQueue()-style isolated queues per test method. Also the natural point to finally migrate SMBScanner onto LibraryRepository — already flagged as unaddressed in sorriva-scanner-handoff-2026-07-25.md §8 ("one more call site for whoever migrates the scanner to the repository"). Not urgent — current temp-file isolation is safe, just not ideal.

features.name: Repeated back-to-back scans cause cascading read failures
features.desc:
2026-07-26: after many consecutive full scans in one session, a rescan failed 445 of 476 files with 'NSPOSIXErrorDomain Code=12 Cannot allocate memory' on the per-file SMBClient login() call. Original suspicion was connection/socket/file-descriptor exhaustion from the fresh-connection-per-file read pattern.

ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED 2026-07-29. THE CAUSE: SMBClient v0.3.1 never calls NWConnection.cancel() anywhere in the library. Session.disconnect() -> connection.disconnect() -> cancel() exists, but nothing in the library ever calls it -- the only occurrence of .disconnect() in the entire source is its own definition at Session.swift:66. SMBClient exposes no public method reaching it, and there is no deinit on Connection, Session, or SMBClient (only TreeAccessor has one). logoff() sends the SMB2 LOGOFF frame and zeroes sessionId, then stops -- leaving the TCP connection open. So every file read leaked one kernel flow entry against a hard per-process ceiling of exactly 512, and Sorriva's readHeader (doing disconnectShare() then logoff()) was doing everything the public API offered while never cancelling a single socket.

Note for the record: a prior session's note claiming 'SMBClient's logoff() -> session.disconnect() -> NWConnection.cancel() was verified in source' was WRONG. That chain does not exist in v0.3.1. A comment in ScanCoordinator.swift still asserts the same false thing and should be corrected.

THE FIX: call client.session.disconnect() on every teardown path in SMBMediaSourceReader -- walk close, auth failure, share-connect failure, and read success. The timeout handler now calls it INSTEAD of logoff(): logoff() sends an SMB2 frame and awaits a response, which on a genuinely hung connection may never arrive, so the very call meant to break the hang could itself hang. disconnect() goes straight to cancel(): synchronous, no round-trip, no live session required. NO FORK NEEDED -- `session` is a public property on SMBClient and Session.disconnect() is public, so the seam was reachable all along.

VERIFICATION, in order:
(1) Raw NWConnection churn (NWConnectionProbe, no SMBClient at all): 600 connect/ready/cancel cycles in 10.7s, ~18ms each, rate never degraded. The OS reclaims flow entries correctly and quickly -- it was never an OS limitation.
(2) SMBClient churn WITHOUT session.disconnect(): failed at exactly connection 512 after 87.3s, ~170ms per cycle, degrading from 2.9s per 25 cycles to 6.8s as the flow table filled.
(3) SMBClient churn WITH session.disconnect(): 600 connections, 80.5s, zero failures, flat rate, and zero session stalls (previously ~1 stall per 90 connections).
(4) Real 673-file scan: completed in 400.8s, 663 tracks, 10 read-skipped, 0 write-failed, ZERO NWError 12. All three artwork passes ran (embedded 21/47, folder 27/47) and the retry scheduler resolved all 10 skips on attempt 1 -- the entire pipeline ran 10 minutes in one process, well past a thousand cumulative connections. The same scan previously died at record ~475.

SUPERSEDED FINDINGS from earlier the same session, kept because they were load-bearing at the time: the long-standing 'UNAS Pro drops sessions after ~2 sequential reads' premise -- the stated justification for the fresh-connection-per-file architecture -- is FALSE. Measured sessions carried 55, 80, 91, and across a 1000-file run 1 to 139 reads, averaging 37. That premise almost certainly came from measurements taken inside already-exhausted processes, where session death and budget exhaustion are indistinguishable from the failure signature. Session reuse with transparent reconnect was also verified working (1000 files on 27 connections, every reconnect succeeding immediately on the file that had just stalled). With the leak fixed, session reuse is now a PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION rather than a survival requirement -- 673 files at ~37 reads/session would cost ~18 connections instead of 673.

STILL OPEN, lower priority now that the ceiling is gone:
- ScanCoordinator.swift has six SMBClient creation sites (folder art pass, embedded art pass, and four reconnect-after-timeout/error paths) that still tear down with disconnectShare() + logoff() and never call session.disconnect(). They use one persistent connection per pass rather than one per file, so they leak a handful rather than hundreds -- the 673-file run completed with them unfixed. Worth fixing for correctness. The false comment about logoff() triggering Session.disconnect() lives here too.
- SMBConnectionCounter (added to MediaSourceReader.swift as instrumentation) never emitted a single line in a run where SCAN, ARTWORK and RETRY all logged normally -- sLog appears unreachable from a plain class outside the actor. Tom's direction: strip it later rather than fix the logging path. Dead weight until then.
- Session stalls are reduced but not eliminated: 20 TIMEOUT lines across the clean run, all 10 resulting skips resolved on retry attempt 1. Transient rather than terminal now.
- The ~512 figure was only ever measured on one iPhone. It is a Network.framework/kernel construct and very likely iOS-wide, but that was never tested. Design guidance stands regardless: treat error 12 as a signal to checkpoint and stop cleanly, never as a threshold to tune against.

features.name: testLocalQueueContextAdvancesOnURIChange intermittently fails
features.desc: 2026-07-26: observed failing repeatedly across an entire scanner test-seam session (ScannerTests.swift:521), unrelated to any scanner/database work done that session. Tests PlaybackContextService.advanceLocalContext advancing to track 2 after simulateURIChange(). Suspected cause: the assertion checks contexts[zoneID]?.track synchronously immediately after calling simulateURIChange, but advanceLocalContext performs its update inside an async Task { @MainActor in ... } — the test can race ahead of that update completing, depending on scheduling. Not confirmed via code reading this session, only inferred from repeated observed failures with no code changes to PlaybackContextService in between. Low priority — does not indicate a product defect, only a test needing an expectation/await instead of an immediate synchronous assertion.

features.name: Zone card doesn't reflect grouping for extended period after group command
features.desc: 2026-07-27: grouped a zone via the app; SOAP commands succeeded (coordinator kept playing correctly) but the newly-grouped zone's card kept showing idle with its previous media for approximately ONE HOUR, not a single missed poll cycle. Self-resolved without any user action while the phone was away/likely locked (coffee break) — consistent with the foreground-refresh path (sorrivaAppDidBecomeActive -> handleNetworkRestored()) correcting what the regular periodic polling loop was not correcting on its own. No log was captured during the actual broken window — the exported log was from after it had already resolved, so root cause is NOT diagnosed, only the symptom and approximate duration are known. groupZone() itself (ZoneDiscoveryService.swift) was read and looks structurally correct on its face — does have a deliberate post-group refresh sequence (sleep 1.5s -> fetchTransportStates -> refreshIdleStates -> sleep 0.5s -> fetchTopology). Suspect candidates, unconfirmed: (1) PlaybackContextService's stateless handleZoneUpdate rewrite has no explicit case for 'zone just joined a group, inherit coordinator's context' — a grouped member's own prior isPlaying/currentTrackURI could persist if Sonos reports lagging/inconsistent transport info for a non-coordinator member vs the actual coordinator; (2) something in the idleState/grace-period handling (added for direct-play, e.g. togglePlayPause/playStation/persistStationPlay) was never extended to the group-join path, so a member's stale idleState could persist through normal polling indefinitely rather than just through one grace window. NEXT TIME THIS OCCURS: export the debug log immediately, WHILE still broken, before doing anything that might trigger a foreground refresh (do not background/foreground the app first) — that log is the missing piece needed to actually diagnose this. ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-07-27, same day it was logged — a fresh reproduction with the debug log captured live (per the instruction left in this record) gave the evidence needed. Two distinct bugs, both real: (1) fetchTopology had six independent call sites (discovery, foreground/network-restored, group, ungroup, transfer) with no concurrency guard — grouping the same zone twice in quick succession could let an older, now-stale topology fetch complete after a newer one and silently overwrite correct group state. Fixed with a single topology-refresh coordinator: at most one fetch in flight, concurrent requests coalesce into one guaranteed follow-up rather than racing. (2) fetchTopology's 'zones = parsed.sorted{...}' unconditionally replaced every zone's entire struct on every refresh — TopologyParser only knows id/name/host/idleState/groupMembers, so every OTHER field (station info, current track, position, volume, grace period) reset to bare defaults on every single topology fetch, not just during grouping. Invisible for an already-idle zone with nothing to lose, but visibly blipped any actively-playing zone's now-playing info to blank before several separate async steps restored it moments later. Fixed by merging fresh topology into existing zones (preserving live state for matching IDs) instead of replacing wholesale.

features.name: MP3 tags lost entirely when embedded cover art pushed declared tag size past 64KB
features.desc: RESOLVED 2026-07-27. Discovered while investigating an unrelated track-length report — Tom noticed the scanner retrying files where the read had succeeded but tags came back empty and correctly questioned whether that was a real read failure or a parser gap. parseID3v2's upfront guard (size + 10 <= data.count) rejected the ENTIRE file whenever the declared ID3 tag size — which includes embedded artwork — exceeded the scanner's 64KB read window, even though the real text frames (TIT2/TALB/TPE2/etc.) almost always sit within the first ~1KB of the tag, comfortably inside that window. Confirmed by replicating the exact Swift parsing logic in Python against a real uploaded MP3's bytes before writing any fix: with the guard removed, all 15 useful frames parsed correctly, and the frame-walking loop's existing per-frame guard already stopped cleanly at the oversized APIC frame on its own — the file-level guard was pure liability, protecting nothing. Unlike the analogous FLAC PICTURE-before-VORBIS_COMMENT gap (fScanFailureUtility / ScannerParsingEdgeCaseTests test 16, left as a documented known limitation since it requires the newer larger-read utility to fix properly), this MP3 case is NOT a rare edge case — any file with embedded cover art over ~64KB (routine output from EAC/dbPoweramp CD rips) was silently losing all tags. Fixed outright by removing the premature guard. New regression test (ID3v2EmbeddedArtTests) uses a real MP3 (uploaded directly during diagnosis, trimmed to 100KB, byte-identical to the original for the first 64KB the scanner actually reads) as its fixture rather than a synthetic one. RECOMMENDATION: run a full library rescan — previously-affected MP3s currently have folder/filename-derived fallback metadata instead of their real tags and will need to be re-read to recover it.

features.name: Test seam for the artwork pass orchestration (folder/embedded/online)
features.desc: 2026-07-27: bArtworkSelectionNotBestWins extracted the two pure, testable pieces (ImageDimensionReader, ArtworkBestWins) into their own files with real coverage (ArtworkSelectionTests.swift, using real generated PNG/JPEG fixtures). The pass orchestration itself — runFolderArtPass, runEmbeddedArtPass, ArtworkCache.fetchArtwork — still talks directly to SMBClient/URLSession with no seam, same situation SMBScanner was in before fScannerIdentityIntegrity's MediaSourceReader work. Mirrors that same pattern: a protocol seam would let the actual pass logic (eligibility, ordering, reconnect/retry handling) run against fixtures instead of a live NAS. Not urgent — the decision logic most likely to have subtle bugs is already covered; this would mainly guard the I/O plumbing around it.

features.name: Artwork review and manual match — surface doubtful covers, let the user choose
features.desc:
2026-07-27, following two confirmed cases of wrong automated iTunes artwork matches (a VA compilation and a single-artist "Greatest Hits" album, both with generic/common titles) — no amount of query tuning can fully guarantee a correct automated match when two different albums share a similar or identical name. Rather than keep trying to make automated matching perfectly reliable, put a human in the loop for the final decision: user sees a low-res or wrong album cover in the library, launches a utility, Sorriva searches one or more sources (Apple/iTunes, Discogs, MusicBrainz CAA per fMusicBrainzCoverArt) for that specific album, presents the candidate results, user picks the correct one (or none) to apply. Distinct from fScanFailureUtility (that's for scans that failed outright with a bigger-read retry — different trigger, different sources, different flow) despite both being Settings-adjacent utilities. Sets artManualOverride on apply, same as existing manual artwork override, so future scans never touch it again.

SCOPED 2026-08-07, after bArtworkArtistQuery.

ENTRY POINT IS A REVIEW LIST, NOT A SEARCH BOX. The user should not have to already know an album is wrong. Rank the library by doubt and present that: match confidence below 1.0, and artwork below a resolution threshold. artworkWidth/artworkHeight already exist (v15), so the resolution axis needs no new data; the confidence axis needs fArtworkProvenance.

CANDIDATES RANKED BY TRACK OVERLAP, NOT TITLE. Measured on Johnny Cash '18 Greatest Hits': title similarity ranked 'Super Hits' first, which shares 22% of the tracks, while 'Greatest Hits: The Sun Records Years' shares 78% and never appeared in the title ranking at all. Comparing the scanned tracklist against a candidate's (lookup?id=&entity=song) costs one call per candidate — too expensive at scan time, trivial for the handful a user is looking at. Present it as '14 of your 18 tracks match this release'. Ranking only: never auto-accept on overlap, because a 78% match is still a different release with different art.

RESOLUTION BEFORE UPSCALING. Measured 2026-08-07: 4 of 5 sampled albums serve 1200x1200 from the same URL that currently requests 600x600 (see fArtworkHigherResolutionFetch). Fetching a genuine original always beats reconstructing one, so exhaust real sources first — Apple at full size, then Cover Art Archive / MusicBrainz, which often holds 1000px+ scans Apple does not.

UPSCALING IS COSMETIC, NOT RESTORATIVE, and carries a hazard specific to this content: generative upscalers invent detail, and on an album cover the detail is usually the band name. A sharpened 300px cover will contain plausible, wrong letterforms. Treat it as smoothing for art that exists nowhere better, never as a repair. On-device Core ML (Real-ESRGAN ports run on iPhone) avoids sending the user's library to a third party and has no per-image cost; hosted services do neither. Claude cannot do this — the Anthropic API has no image generation or upscaling endpoint.

Additional sources and upscaling are scoped separately in fArtworkSourcingAndEnhancement — including the on-device-versus-hosted decision and the text-hallucination hazard — so that a Core ML model choice is not buried inside a UI ticket.

OVERLAPS fArtworkManagement: 'pick from search results' and 'supply your own image' are two doors into one room and should almost certainly be one screen.

features.name: Embedded art retry loop never resolves a confirmed 'no art' result
features.desc: RESOLVED 2026-07-27. Same bug class as an earlier scan_skips fix (retrying a confirmed negative result forever instead of accepting it as final). The retry loop's 'no art in file' branch (a successful read, genuinely no embedded art) called markEmbeddedArtScanned, which only set embeddedArtScanned=1 — but the retry queue's own eligibility query (albumsNeedingEmbeddedArtRetry) filters on a DIFFERENT flag, embeddedArtFailed, which was never cleared. Real repro: an album retried indefinitely showing 'attempt 2/5' without ever incrementing, since nothing in the no-art branch touched either flag the retry queue actually depends on. Fixed by having markEmbeddedArtScanned clear embeddedArtFailed too, matching its actual intent (no further scanning OR retrying needed) everywhere it's called, not just this one call site.

features.name: A failed tag read created a track/album from empty fallback data instead of skipping
features.desc: RESOLVED 2026-07-27. When a file's header read failed, the scanner still fell through to buildTrack with an empty ParsedMetadata, relying on fillFromPath's folder-name fallback. For the first track scanned in a folder, this meant a transient NAS read timeout (not a genuine content issue) could permanently create the ALBUM with wrong data — real repro: 'Various Artists - 12 Inch Dance 80s Remix (CD 2)' track 1 timed out, fillFromPath ran with no artist context (both albumArtist and artist were nil), couldn't correctly strip the folder name's 'Various Artists - ' prefix, and created the album under the wrong, unstripped name. Worse: the retry pass later successfully re-read the SAME file's tags correctly, but only ever updates a track's own row — it never propagates corrected data back to fix an album record that was already wrongly created upstream, so the bad album persisted even after the underlying read issue resolved itself. Tom identified the structurally correct fix: a failed read should never create anything from empty data in the first place — just record the skip and move on, so whichever read succeeds first (this pass or on retry) is what defines the track and album. Implemented by moving buildTrack/write inside the read-succeeded branch only; FolderStat and progress bookkeeping stayed unconditional so a folder containing a skip can still complete once retry resolves it, rather than never completing.

features.name: Automated change detection cannot see new folders
features.desc:
findChangedFolders iterates folderStats(sourceId:) -- the folders already recorded in the DB -- and re-counts each one. It never walks the tree. So a newly added album folder has no folder_stats row, is never in the loop, is never checked, and is never scanned: new music on the NAS does not appear in the library until a manual full rescan. Found 2026-07-29 while designing the unified scan model. Fixed structurally by walk-then-filter (HANDOFF-scanner-architecture-2026-07-29.md item 3): the walk enumerates what is actually on disk, and absence of a stat means 'scan it', never 'skip it'. That change retires findChangedFolders entirely.

FIXED 2026-07-30 by fUnifiedScanWalkThenFilter. The walk now enumerates what is actually on disk, and absence of a stat means 'scan it' rather than being invisible. VERIFIED: app quit, folder added to the NAS, relaunch -- the foreground change check reported '2 new folder(s)' and scanned them with no manual action.

features.name: tracks.filePath is globally unique, not scoped by source
features.desc:
t.column("filePath", .text).notNull().unique() -- uniqueness is on the path alone, NOT (sourceId, filePath). Paths are share-relative (rootPath + walk path); host and share are never concatenated in. So two sources covering the same relative path produce ONE track row whose sourceId flips to whichever scanned last (upsertTrackIdempotent finds by filePath and updates). Combined with onDelete: .cascade on tracks.sourceId, REMOVING THE SHARE THAT SCANNED LAST DELETES TRACKS THE OTHER SHARE STILL COVERS ON DISK -- silently, no error, recoverable only by full rescan. Playback is also affected: the row's sourceId resolves to host and credentials, so after the second source scans, Sonos gets an x-file-cifs:// URI for the wrong machine.

This is a hard blocker on any second library source (fMacBridge, a second NAS). Correct key is (host, share, filePath), which is what WP-12 meant by 'file paths are not used as application-level identity'.

Mitigated for the single-server case by share-overlap prevention (HANDOFF item 7) rather than fixed -- that makes same-server overlap impossible, so the cascade is unreachable. Fully-qualified paths were considered and deliberately deferred: they require rewriting every existing track and album path, reworking Sonos URI construction (which currently concatenates host + share + filePath and would double-prefix), and requalifying folder_stats.

Cheaper partial mitigation if ever needed sooner: make upsertTrackIdempotent first-writer-wins on sourceId (do not overwrite it on an existing row). No migration. Still wrong if the FIRST share is removed instead of the last.

features.name: album lookup by folderPath is global, not scoped by source
features.desc:
album(folderPath:) filters on the path string only -- no host, share or sourceId. Combined with albums.sourceId being a single NOT NULL column, an album physically cannot reference two sources. Two sources with the same relative path therefore share one album owned by whichever scanned first, and that album is invisible to the other source's artwork passes and scan report (both select via albums(sourceId:)) -- this is what fOverlappingShareDetection meant by 'produces 0 tracks in its report'.

Note this same mechanism is CORRECT and desirable for nested shares on one server: two shares whose folderPath strings coincide resolving to one album is the intended 'one folder is one album' behaviour. The defect is only that it cannot distinguish two different servers. Same class as bTrackFilePathGloballyUnique; blocks multi-source. If one-album-many-sources is ever wanted, that is an album_sources join table or the WP-12 canonical model.

features.name: Interrupted artwork phase never restarts
features.desc:
Quitting the app during the artwork phase loses that work permanently. Backgrounding is fine -- the same process resumes the same task -- but a quit destroys it, and NOTHING except a scan ever starts the artwork passes: they only run inside runScan's pipeline task. After a completed file scan, checkForChanges takes the 'complete' branch, finds no changed folders, and does nothing. Confirmed in a real log: launch, checkForChanges fires, not a single SCAN line follows.

Per-pass state today: embedded has a permanent per-album marker (embeddedArtScanned); folder pass has NO marker and restarts from album 1 every time; online uses artPathThumb == nil, so albums with no findable art retry forever.

Fix agreed 2026-07-29 (HANDOFF-scanner-architecture-2026-07-29.md item 5): per-album markers for all three passes with FolderStat semantics -- the marker means 'done for this scan', reset only for albums in the folders being scanned, never reset on resume, artManualOverride skipped permanently. Plus resumeArtworkIfNeeded(source:) on the 'complete' branch so an interrupted artwork phase resumes without needing a scan. Must NOT gate on albumsWithoutArtwork() -- some albums never have findable art, so that count never reaches zero and the pass would re-run on every foreground.

FIXED 2026-07-30. All three passes are marker-driven with FolderStat semantics. v17 adds folderArtScanned and onlineArtAttempted; embeddedArtScanned changes from permanent to per-scan. Markers are reset at scan start for exactly the folders being scanned -- never the whole source -- so an incremental scan of 2 folders re-evaluates 2 albums, not all of them. Resume never resets, so an interrupted phase continues.

Marking happens via `defer` in the folder pass and after the attempt in the online pass, NOT at the top of the iteration. Tom caught this: marking up front treats an album killed mid-check as done and silently skips its artwork. defer runs on normal completion and on every `continue` exit (manual override, no folder path, reconnect-after-timeout, no winner, no winner path) but never when the process is killed -- so a considered album is always marked and an interrupted one is always retried.

runArtworkPasses extracted so the passes can run outside a scan, and checkForChanges calls it when hasPendingArtworkWork is true. Previously the passes existed only inside the scan pipeline, so quitting during artwork lost that work with no way back in: the file scan was already complete, so the next foreground found nothing to do.

Online selection deliberately KEEPS the hard artPathThumb == nil gate, preserving the 2026-07-27 revert -- iTunes always claims 600x600, so area comparison cannot tell a right match from a wrong one, and a wrong match must never overwrite correct folder artwork. The marker only stops albums with no findable art being re-queried forever.

VERIFIED: rescan of an unchanged share reports 'nothing to scan' for all three passes; a rescan with 1 new folder runs embedded [1/1] and folder [1/1] rather than [1/13]; killed during embedded at [4/13] resumed at [1/9] and killed during folder at [3/13] resumed at [1/11] -- remainder plus the interrupted album, in both cases.

features.name: Prevent or absorb overlapping library shares
features.desc:
Agreed 2026-07-29 as the cheap alternative to fully-qualified paths. Rules at share-add time, using host, share and rootPath: new share INSIDE an existing one on the same host+share -> block, already covered; new share CONTAINING an existing one -> offer absorb; same relative rootPath on a DIFFERENT host -> warn only (legitimate backup case, rare); no overlap -> proceed. Prefix comparison needs a trailing-separator guard so /Music does not falsely match /Music II.

ABSORB: adding a share at the root when a narrow share exists deeper is legitimate expansion, not an error. It is nearly free because the path strings already coincide -- rootPath is embedded in the path the walk builds, so both shares produce identical folderPath values. Existing rows are already valid; only sourceId is wrong. In ONE transaction, reassign albums/tracks/folder_stats/scan_skips to the new sourceId, clear currentScanSessionId, then delete the old library_sources row -- IN THAT ORDER, because onDelete: .cascade on both albums.sourceId and tracks.sourceId would otherwise take everything with it. Then scan normally; carried-over folder_stats mean walk-then-filter skips the already-scanned subtree.

currentScanSessionId MUST be cleared: carried-over folder_stats rows carry the old share's session id, and resuming against it would filter using a session that scanned a different tree. Worst case after clearing is a full rescan of an already-correct library -- slow, never wrong.

PRECONDITION: block absorb if either share has scanState == 'scanning', with a message to let it finish or cancel. Absorbing mid-scan silently discards in-flight work.

Why this instead of qualified paths: the only reason to create a second share into the same tree is to rescan a changed album, and under the unified scan model finding one changed album in 10k tracks takes well under a minute (walk ~25-30s extrapolated from 673 files in 1.7s, in-memory filter, ~8s for the one folder). The targeted share has no purpose, so preventing same-server overlap makes the whole class of cascade problem unreachable.

features.name: Unified scan model — walk the tree, skip unchanged folders
features.desc:
Agreed 2026-07-29, replaces the full-scan/incremental split. ONE primitive: walk the tree, skip folders whose stored stat still matches (file count + total bytes + newest modification time), scan the rest. Manual scan, automatic foreground scan and resume all use it; they differ only in trigger, and in what resume additionally skips.

Replaces two paths: the full scan (folderPaths == nil), which reads EVERY header with no stat comparison at all -- a manual rescan of 13.5k tracks re-reads everything, roughly two hours, even if nothing changed -- and findChangedFolders, which iterates the DB rather than the disk and therefore cannot see new folders at all (bNewFoldersNotDetected).

Requires modification time through the reader seam. VERIFIED AVAILABLE: SMBClient.File exposes public var lastWriteTime: Date (Sources/SMBClient/SMBClient.swift:281), no fork needed. MediaSourceEntry gains modifiedAt; both SMBMediaSourceReader and FixtureMediaSourceReader map it. mtime is NOT optional -- it is what closes bTagEditsNotDetected (taggers write into the FLAC PADDING block, so neither count nor bytes changes) and, more importantly, once manual and automatic share the same skip logic, the old de facto workaround of 'manual rescan re-reads everything' disappears.

Also includes deletion reconciliation: the walk produces the complete disk picture, so storedPaths - walkedPaths identifies deleted folders, whose tracks and stats today persist forever. VERIFIED SAFE -- both folderStats(sourceId:) and the DELETE are sourceId-scoped, so shares cannot affect each other's rows. Only valid on full-tree walks; must be skipped if any folder-scoped scan is ever reintroduced.

Compute totalFiles AFTER filtering or progress reports against the wrong denominator. The resume filter built for fScanResume is the same shape and should be folded into this one code path rather than kept separate. Full detail in HANDOFF-scanner-architecture-2026-07-29.md items 1-4.

BUILT AND VERIFIED 2026-07-30. One primitive now serves manual scan, automatic foreground scan and resume: walk the tree, group by folder, skip folders whose stored FolderFingerprint still matches (file count + total bytes + newest mtime), scan the rest. Resume adds one condition -- the folder must also carry the resumed session's stamp. findChangedFolders, startIncrementalScan, collectAudioFilesPublic and SMBClientListingOnlyReader all deleted; they existed only to serve the old incremental path. Modification time reaches the seam via MediaSourceEntry.modifiedAt, mapped from SMBClient.File.lastWriteTime in production and real filesystem mtime in the fixture reader. FolderFingerprint holds the match rule in one place so the write path and the skip decision cannot drift. A NULL stored mtime counts as changed, so pre-v17 rows are rescanned once rather than silently trusted. Deletion reconciliation included: storedPaths - walkedPaths identifies folders gone from disk and removes their tracks and stats, guarded to full-tree walks and sourceId-scoped throughout. VERIFIED: initial scan 104 files/9 folders in 37s; immediate rescan 0.6s with all 104 skipped; 2 new folders detected and only their 25 files scanned; a deleted folder reconciled and its album cleaned up; and the foreground change check picked up 2 new folders with no user action.

features.name: Directory walk needs reconnect-on-stall handling
features.desc:
connectedWalkClient() holds ONE SMB connection across the entire directory walk. At 673 files that completed in 1.7s with no trouble; at ~10k files / ~1000 listDirectory calls it is untested. Session 2026-07-29 established that SMB sessions die unpredictably -- measured 1 to 139 reads before a stall, averaging 37, with no correlation to read count, bytes transferred or elapsed time. The walk needs the same treatment readHeader has: timeout, session.disconnect(), fresh client, retry the failed listDirectory, continue. Build it in rather than discovering it at 10k.

BUILT 2026-07-31. listDirectory retries up to 3 times, each on a fresh connection, with a 10s stall ceiling per attempt; on timeout it force-cancels via session.disconnect(), discards the client and reconnects. 10s rather than 15 because a listing returns metadata only — on a healthy connection it completes in milliseconds, so anything near the ceiling is a dead session, and shorter waits matter across ~1000 folders.

NOT YET EXERCISED. The full 11,670-file scan the same night produced zero 'walk recovered on attempt N' lines — one connection survived all 562 listDirectory calls. So the retry is correct by construction but unproven in practice. Kept because the walk runs before any file is read: a single mid-walk stall fails the entire scan with no partial result and nothing for resume to pick up.

features.name: Retry scheduler hammers a failing NAS with no backoff
features.desc: Observed 2026-07-29: after connection exhaustion the retry scheduler fired hundreds of doomed retries, cycling the same file list repeatedly, burning further connection attempts for zero possible gain and deepening the hole it was trying to climb out of. No circuit breaker exists. Needs: N consecutive failures of the same class -> stop, surface an actionable message, do not keep hammering. Gate-relevant under 'critical failures produce actionable diagnostics' -- the retry noise actively buries real signal in the log.

features.name: findChangedFolders leaks one connection per foreground check
features.desc: Its defer blocks tear down with logoff() and disconnectShare() only, never session.disconnect() -- so NWConnection.cancel() is never reached and one kernel flow entry leaks on every foreground change detection. Same root cause as bScanConnectionExhaustionOnRepeatedScans; this specific call site was not covered by that fix because it uses a different call shape. Becomes moot once fUnifiedScanWalkThenFilter retires findChangedFolders, so fix there rather than separately.

features.name: PlaybackContextService re-resolves the same zone hundreds of times per second
features.desc: Observed 2026-07-29 in a real log: 'CONTEXT: resolved idle station' fires hundreds of times within a single second at launch, repeatedly for the same zone id. Harmless functionally but it is write-side heuristic recomputation on every topology update, and it floods the debug log at exactly the moment launch diagnostics matter most. Likely folds into the PlaybackStore write-side architecture conversation (HANDOFF-playbackstore-architecture.md) rather than being worth fixing standalone.

features.name: 'folder done' logged enumerated files, not persisted tracks
features.desc: The scan log line printed folderFiles.count -- the ENUMERATED file count -- so a folder where every read failed still logged its full track count. Real case 2026-07-29: folders logging 'folder done (10 tracks)' while all 10 reads failed with NWError 12, and the folder-done lines summing to ~50 against a scan total of 14 tracks. This invalidated the diagnostic bMissingTracksInAlbum's own investigation notes call for. FIXED 2026-07-29 -- now reports written vs enumerated with an explicit shortfall: 'folder done (11 of 12 tracks written, 1 missing)'.

features.name: A hang in the post-scan pipeline was permanent
features.desc:
scanState -> 'retrying' and activeScanSourceId = nil both happen AFTER the artwork passes, inside the same detached task. So a stall during artwork left the app permanently believing a scan was healthy and running: no alert, no resume, a live ScanStatusPanel forever, the retry scheduler never ran, and it also blocked the new killed-scan detection (which correctly reads activeScanSourceId being set as 'running'). Observed 2026-07-29: folder art pass stopped mid-album-10 when the app was backgrounded and never resumed across two foregrounds and fifteen minutes, with none of its own timeouts firing.

FIXED 2026-07-29: lastPipelineProgress heartbeat updated by the scan progress callback and by every artwork album iteration; the previously-unheld pipelineTask captured so detached artwork work can actually be cancelled; a 240s stall threshold in checkForChanges that cancels both tasks, restores the idle timer, sets 'error' and offers resume. 240s is deliberately generous -- a slow album read plus reconnect can legitimately exceed a minute and a false positive interrupts real work.

NOT YET VERIFIED. Test: start a scan, reach the folder art pass, background 5 minutes, foreground -- expect 'SCAN: pipeline WEDGED'.

features.name: Tag scan pipeline log lines with the run's session id
features.desc:
A scan writes under three prefixes -- SCAN, ARTWORK and RETRY -- with nothing tying them to a run, and neither Console's filter nor a text search can express 'SCAN or ARTWORK or RETRY'. Following one scan meant three separate searches and manual interleaving by timestamp.

BUILT 2026-07-30. Format is 'SCAN [3A10C9D2]: message' -- category first so existing search habits still work and the log still reads in aligned columns, session id after it. Searching SCAN still finds scan lines, 3A10C9D2 finds the whole run, 'ARTWORK [3A10C9D2]' finds one phase of one run. Implemented centrally in SorrivaLogger.log via ScanLogSession.decorate, so all four emitting files were covered with no call-site changes; only the three pipeline categories are tagged, leaving ZONES/CONTEXT/PROBE untouched. The window opens at scan start and closes at pipeline end, including the failure path.

A resumed scan reuses the interrupted run's session id, so one search spans the original attempt, the kill and the resume. VERIFIED across a sequence of three kills and resumes: session E3A7AD93 appears on every line across four app launches.

features.name: Debug log rotated on every launch, discarding crash and kill evidence
features.desc:
SorrivaLogger.openLog() rotated the log on every app launch, moving everything to sorriva-debug-prev.log and opening an empty file. That discarded the log at exactly the moment it mattered most -- relaunching after a crash or kill -- so exporting immediately after an interruption showed nothing but the relaunch. Diagnostics that erase themselves on failure are worse than none, because they look like evidence that nothing happened. This made every kill/resume test unobservable and cost real debugging time on 2026-07-29 and 2026-07-30.

Writes were also unflushed, so anything still in the file buffer was lost when the process died.

FIXED 2026-07-30: rotation is size-driven only (256KB, already handled in write()); launches append a '===== APP LAUNCH =====' marker instead. Every write now synchronize()s to disk. VERIFIED: a single log spanning ten launches and three app kills, with all pre-kill entries intact. Gate-relevant under 'critical failures produce actionable diagnostics'.

features.name: Scanner marked scanState 'idle' before the artwork passes ran
features.desc:
SorrivaDatabase.updateScanComplete hardcoded scanState = 'idle' alongside the counts update, so the scanner declared the whole pipeline finished the moment the FILE pass ended -- before the artwork passes had even started. Two consequences: a kill during artwork left the source at 'idle', which matched no branch in checkForChanges, so no interrupted-scan alert appeared and the work was lost silently; and any source left at 'idle' fell through to `default: break`, so change detection never ran for it again. Killing during the FILE pass worked fine, which is why this hid for so long -- that path leaves 'scanning'.

FIXED 2026-07-30: updateScanComplete owns counts and fingerprint only. scanState is ScanCoordinator's across the whole pipeline. A recovery branch was added for sources stranded at 'idle' by earlier builds.

features.name: Scan Incomplete alert only appeared intermittently
features.desc:
SorrivaAppEnvironment declares `@Published var scanCoordinator: ScanCoordinator = .shared`, but @Published on a reference type fires only when the REFERENCE changes -- never, since it is assigned once. Mutating interruptedScanSource fired objectWillChange on ScanCoordinator, which nothing observed, so the alert binding was never re-evaluated.

It appeared intermittently, which made it look like a detection bug rather than a rendering one: any unrelated publish on `environment` triggered a re-render that then found the non-nil value. Proven by a repro where the same pending state produced no alert on a cold relaunch and then appeared on a later foreground with nothing having changed in between.

FIXED 2026-07-30 by extracting the alert into a ViewModifier holding @ObservedObject var coordinator: ScanCoordinator -- the same pattern ContentView already documents for tabState, discovery and playbackStore.

features.name: Foreground change check launched overlapping scans across sources
features.desc:
checkForChanges loops every source and, after fUnifiedScanWalkThenFilter, calls a full scan for each one that is 'complete'. There is a single scanTask property, so each call silently overwrote the previous handle and `await scanTask?.value` waited on whichever was current rather than the one just started -- the loop raced ahead launching more. Observed 2026-07-30: seven sources produced four different activeScanSourceId values within 130ms, clobbering each other and leaving sources in 'error'. The old code only reached this path for sources with detected changes, so it rarely fired more than once.

FIXED 2026-07-30: the loop breaks entirely if any scan is active. Whatever is not reached is picked up on the next foreground.

features.name: Never-scanned shares started importing themselves on foreground
features.desc:
'idle' is both the state a stranded scan leaves behind AND the schema default for a newly added source, so a recovery branch that promoted stranded 'idle' sources to 'complete' also promoted shares that had never been scanned. The change check then found no folder_stats, classified every folder as new, and began a full 673-file import triggered by a foreground rather than by the user.

FIXED 2026-07-30 with hasBeenScanned(source), true only when the source has recorded at least one folder. All three branches ('idle', 'error', 'complete') now enforce the same rule: a never-scanned source does nothing automatically. Initial scans stay user-initiated. A source at 'error' with no stats is reset to idle rather than offered for resume, since there is nothing to resume TO.

features.name: Read-failure skip records were batched and lost when a scan was killed
features.desc:
Read failures accumulated in memory and were written to scan_skips only after the entire file loop finished, so a kill mid-scan lost every one recorded so far. Worse under resume: a folder gets its FolderStat when all its files are CONSIDERED -- skips included -- so on resume that folder is skipped, the failed files are never retried, and the records that would have driven retry were never written. The track is silently absent with nothing pointing at it. Write failures were already persisted immediately; only read failures batched.

FIXED 2026-07-30: skips are written the moment they occur. The batching saved one transaction per scan against 2-18 rows, which is not worth losing the queue to an interruption.

features.name: Interrupted-scan dialog offered for automatic change checks the user never started
features.desc:
Since fUnifiedScanWalkThenFilter, checkForChanges starts a full scan for every 'complete' source on every foreground. Those scans are usually sub-second no-ops, but runScan writes scanState = 'scanning' before doing anything, so the window in which a kill produces an interrupted-scan state is now much wider -- and most of those scans are automatic change checks, not user actions.

The result is a 'the scan did not complete' dialog offering Resume/Start Over for a scan the user never started and which did no work. An interrupted change check needs no user decision; it should simply run again on the next foreground. The distinction is available -- a run that filtered to zero files did nothing worth resuming -- so the fix is to record whether the run actually scanned anything and only offer the dialog when it did.

Raised by Tom 2026-07-30 while testing; deliberately not fixed mid-test-run to avoid adding a variable during verification of items 1-5.

FIXED 2026-08-01, dissolved rather than patched. The session records BOTH its trigger (manual/automatic/resume) and what it planned, so an interrupted automatic run with plannedFiles == 0 is cancelled silently — there is nothing to resume and the user never asked for it. No special case required; it falls out of the session having identity.

features.name: Artwork-only resume is reachable only by tapping Cancel on the interrupted-scan dialog
features.desc:
CORRECTED 2026-08-01. This record originally claimed Cancel was the ONLY route to artwork resume. That was inferred from reading the branch structure, not observed, and the 2026-07-30 Test C contradicts it — killing during embedded art and tapping Resume worked correctly, because a full-scan resume filters to zero files and lands in the artwork passes anyway.

The real issue is narrower and cosmetic: the Scan Incomplete dialog appears when only artwork is outstanding, which needs no user decision. hasPendingArtworkWork already answers that question, so the passes could simply continue without asking. Lowered to Low.

features.name: Version numbers drift between version.json and the git history
features.desc:
The version is assigned when the session-close manifest is written, but the Swift push happens separately and sometimes carries a different number, with no single source of truth. Observed 2026-07-30: the 2026-07-29 session recorded 0.0.48 in version.json and sessions.json, but that work was pushed to git as part of 0.0.49; then this session's Swift commit reused 0.0.49 as well, so two distinct commits (d398080 and 3d00c18) carry the same version string. Resolved by moving this session to 0.0.50 rather than rewriting history.

Candidate fix: have gitops read the version from version.json and pre-fill it in the commit prompt, so the repo and the state files cannot disagree.

features.name: Artwork retry read had no timeout — hung the pipeline permanently
features.desc:
ScanRetryScheduler.retryFailedEmbeddedArt awaited reader.read() with no stall ceiling. SMBClient's async methods never check for cancellation, so an unresponsive read is not slow, it is permanent.

Observed 2026-07-31: a full 11,670-file scan completed successfully, then stalled on the FIRST album of the art retry and sat there. Every relaunch reproduced it, because scanState 'retrying' restarts the scheduler, which hit the same album and stalled again — unrecoverable without clearing the library. The pipeline wedge watchdog could not help either: lastPipelineProgress was only updated by the scan progress callback and the artwork album loops, so from the watchdog's point of view the retry scheduler did not exist. And no interrupted-scan alert appeared, because that requires scanState 'scanning' and this is 'retrying'.

FIXED 2026-07-31: 15s ceiling with session.disconnect() on timeout (the only call reaching NWConnection.cancel(); logoff() would send a frame and await a response on a connection unresponsive by definition). Heartbeat added per album via notePipelineProgressExternal() so the watchdog can see the retry pass at all.

features.name: Retry scheduler leaked a connection per pass
features.desc: Three teardown sites in ScanRetryScheduler called logoff() without session.disconnect() — end of pass, the mid-loop reconnect path, and the early-return path. logoff() sends the SMB2 LOGOFF frame and zeroes sessionId while leaving the TCP connection open, so each retry pass leaked kernel flow entries against the hard ~512 per-process ceiling (bScanConnectionExhaustionOnRepeatedScans). Same omission as the original bug, in a file that was not covered when that fix went in. FIXED 2026-07-31.

features.name: RETRY log lines lost their session tag mid-run
features.desc:
Two causes. The scheduler outlives the scan pipeline and can be restarted independently after a kill, so it had no way to re-establish the tag — RETRY lines after a relaunch carried no session id and could not be searched alongside the scan that produced their queue. And ScanCoordinator's pipeline completion called ScanLogSession.end() immediately after starting the scheduler, racing it and stripping the tag off everything after the first two lines.

FIXED 2026-07-31: the scheduler reads currentScanSessionId at start and calls ScanLogSession.begin; the pipeline no longer ends the session; the scheduler clears both the tag and the stored session id when it genuinely completes, which is the real end of the run.

FIXED 2026-08-01 by two changes. ScanLogSession became @TaskLocal, bound around the whole run and rebound inside the detached pipeline task (Task.detached deliberately does not inherit task-locals). And the two session identifiers were collapsed into one — see bScanSessionIdDuplication. Verified: a single id across scan, artwork, retry and both LEDGER lines.

features.name: Scan session ledger — record the plan, account for every outcome
features.desc:
THE central open item for the scanner. Full design in HANDOFF-scan-session-ledger-2026-07-31.md.

A scan session should be a bounded, auditable unit of work: it records what it intended to do, records every outcome against that intent, and is not complete until every planned item has reached a terminal state. Today it is none of those things — the session id exists but nothing is attributed to it, the retry scheduler is a separate actor that happens to run afterward, nothing records what the scan intended, and completion is a scanState string written by four different code paths.

WHAT PROMPTED IT: the 2026-07-31 full-library scan produced 11,231 tracks with 439 skipped; retry recovered 419, leaving 20 tracks and 5 albums outstanding. The scheduler then hung, and after a relaunch both queues eventually read as empty with no log line saying the work had been done. Nobody could say what happened to those 20 tracks and 5 albums — not the user, not the log, not Claude reading the log. That uncertainty is the defect; the specific bugs are downstream of it.

Tom's framing: 'this would also allow a user to see specifically what failed rather than saying 20 of your 11,000 tracks didn't make it. have fun trying to figure out which ones.' The app currently cannot tell a user WHICH tracks are missing, and cannot tell them anything is missing at all — an album showing 12 tracks looks like a 12-track album.

AGREED RULES: the retry phase is part of the session, not a separate process; no other scan of that share runs until the session completes or is cancelled; interrupted retries recover exactly as interrupted tracks and artwork do; the record survives automatic scans and is cleared only by a manual scan of that same share; albums, tracks AND artwork are all auditable.

THE ARITHMETIC: planned = written + skipped-resolved + skipped-permanent + unaccounted. Any non-zero unaccounted is a bug, and it names the exact files. Failure REASON must be recorded, not just failure — all 439 skips that night were timeouts, which are very likely recoverable, and that is a different user message and a different retry policy from a corrupt file or a permission error.

BUILT AND VERIFIED 2026-08-01. v18 added scan_sessions and scan_ledger (one row per planned file, carrying outcome, failure kind and attempt count). v19 added `kind` and `resolvedBy` so artwork joins the SAME table rather than getting a parallel one — Tom's call, on the grounds that separate tables would reintroduce exactly the duplication being removed. scan_skips is retired as the retry queue; nothing outside SorrivaDatabase reads it.

Retry is now part of the session rather than a separate actor with its own lifecycle, and completeness is one query over one table (sessionHasOutstandingWork) covering tracks and artwork together. Failure REASON is recorded, which is what lets a timeout and a corrupt file get different retry policies and different user-facing messages.

DEVICE REGRESSION, four phases on a 159-file / 14-folder share, UNACCOUNTED 0 on every audit line in every phase. Phase 2 is the one that matters: FIVE kills across three pipeline phases — twice during the track scan, twice during artwork, once mid-file during retry — with the session id constant throughout and each resume picking up the exact remainder. Artwork killed at [4/14] resumed at [1/10]; killed at [10/14] resumed at [1/5]; retry killed mid-file resumed with 1 pending, not 6. Final audits totalled 173 (159 track + 14 artwork) across all interruptions.

One detail worth keeping: after the first kill the folder filter reported 137 files to scan while the ledger reported 126 still planned. The 11-file difference is the ledger being finer-grained than the folder filter — those 11 were already written in a folder that had not completed. That is what makes resume exact rather than approximate.

Steps 6-8 of HANDOFF-scan-session-ledger.md remain open and are tracked as fScanReportShareExport, fScanFailureRecoveryTool and bAlbumMissingTracksNotVisible.

features.name: Write a human-readable scan report to the share after each session
features.desc:
Agreed 2026-07-31. The DB stays authoritative — the audit's job is to answer 'what's missing', and the most likely reason something is missing is that the NAS was unreachable, so a ledger living only on the NAS is unavailable exactly when it is needed. It is also a query, not a document, and it drives the inline '12 of 15 tracks' signal which must be instant on a scroll.

But a report should be WRITTEN to the share when a session reaches terminal state. One connection, one write, after the fact — never during the scan, which would consume the connection budget being tested and fail precisely when diagnostics matter.

This is a first-class feature, not a developer convenience. Tom: 'its not about the mini. its about some future user who doesn't have a mini.' For a user with no second machine the share is the only place they can reach a file from a computer they are already sitting at — they already have the NAS mounted, because that is how the music got there. The Settings → share sheet → AirDrop → find-it-in-Downloads flow is a developer's workaround.

Which means the FORMAT matters: a human opens this directly. Not a JSON dump — album, tracks that did not import, and why, readable in TextEdit by someone who knows nothing about the app's internals. Same mechanism answers debug log retention generally (see fLogTransportAndRetention).

features.name: Library Management — review scan failures and retry them in place
features.desc:
Agreed 2026-07-31. Supersedes fScanFailureUtility, which was scoped as a Settings screen without a ledger underneath it to make it possible.

Review the session record and recover from it on the same screen. The machinery largely exists: scan_skips holds exact file paths, the retry scheduler already knows how to re-read a single file, and folderPath gives album-level scope. Three actions: retry this track, retry this album, retry everything.

The difference from today's automatic retry is that it is user-initiated and REPORTS BACK. Today it runs invisibly on a backoff schedule and the user finds out by noticing a track missing months later.

Surface the failure REASON so the user knows whether retrying is worth anything before they tap it — '12 tracks timed out, likely recoverable' versus '1 track unreadable, check the file'. Depends on fScanSessionLedger.

features.name: An album with failed reads is indistinguishable from a short album
features.desc: An album showing 12 tracks looks like a 12-track album. There is no marker distinguishing 'this album has 12 tracks' from 'three reads failed and those tracks are simply absent'. The user has no way to know anything is missing, let alone what. Raised 2026-07-31 while designing fScanSessionLedger, which is what would make the inline signal possible — the ledger knows the planned track count per folder, so '12 of 15' can be shown at the point the user actually encounters the album.

features.name: resetArtworkPassMarkers silently empties the artwork retry queue
features.desc:
resetArtworkPassMarkers (added 2026-07-30 for bArtworkPassNotResumable) zeroes embeddedArtFailed along with the three pass markers. But embeddedArtFailed is the column albumsNeedingEmbeddedArtRetry() selects on — so any scan touching those folders silently empties the artwork retry queue rather than working it. The albums are not retried, they are dropped, with no log line because nothing processed them.

Probable cause of 5 albums vanishing from the retry queue during the 2026-07-31 full-library run, though not proven: the scan that would have cleared them filtered to zero files, so the reset should not have run. The inability to establish this from the record is itself the argument for fScanSessionLedger.

A narrow fix (exclude embeddedArtFailed from the reset) was proposed and REJECTED as symptom-patching. The real issue is that retry state and pass state are conflated: the three markers mean 'not yet done this scan', while embeddedArtFailed means 'a read errored and this is queued for retry'. The ledger resolves this properly by making retry part of the session rather than a parallel queue.

FIXED 2026-08-01, dissolved rather than patched. The narrow fix (exclude embeddedArtFailed from the reset) was proposed and REJECTED as symptom-patching. Artwork now lives in the ledger via v19's `kind` column, where resetArtworkPassMarkers cannot reach it — the session's view of outstanding artwork is a ledger query, not a parallel queue another component can clobber.

features.name: Header read timeout of 15s costs most of a full scan's runtime
features.desc:
Measured 2026-07-31 on the full library: 439 timeouts x 15s = 110 minutes of a 3h03m header pass, roughly 60% of total runtime spent waiting on reads that never return. At 5s the same run would have spent ~37 minutes.
