  2. ZoneDiscoveryService is the real coupling: discovery, polling, cache and orchestration, all Sonos-specific, and already mid-decomposition (fZoneDiscoveryServiceDecomposition). Something must merge endpoints from several drivers into one list.
  3. Routing. SonosCommands.play*(on: SonosZone) sends SOAP. A local endpoint needs a different path entirely — and for local FLAC, Sorriva has never had a local player at all. That is real work, not a setting.

AIRPLAY DUPLICATES NATIVE ENDPOINTS, and this is Tom's insight, 2026-08-21. Sonos and Bluesound advertise themselves BOTH natively and over AirPlay, so a naive endpoint list shows every speaker twice. His rule: SUPPRESS the AirPlay entry for any device already present natively — the native protocol is richer and is what grouping, queues and play modes are built on.

BUT AIRPLAY IS ALSO THE BRIDGE, which is why it cannot simply be filtered away. Sonos cannot group with Bluesound natively; AirPlay is the only common denominator. So the rule has an exception with teeth: when the user groups endpoints of DIFFERENT topologies, that group becomes an AirPlay zone and the suppressed AirPlay identity is exactly what makes it possible. Suppression is therefore presentational, not a discard — the AirPlay identity of a native endpoint must be RETAINED and reachable.

UNVERIFIED, do not assume: that Sonos and Bluesound both advertise over AirPlay in this household, how their AirPlay identity maps to their native one, and whether an AirPlay group spanning vendors behaves well enough to ship. All three are measurable on the real speakers before any of this is designed further — the same discipline that settled the Apple Music addresses.

features.name: Storage/Library split — closed as no change needed, the structure was already right
features.desc:
Local Library is plumbing; Library Management is content; the two are currently tangled. Tom, 2026-08-07: 'this area of settings is to add shares so networking focused. scanning is library focused.'

THE LINE. Services = streaming sources. Storage = your own files. Library = what came out of both. Each screen owns one idea.

IN SCOPE — ONE STORAGE SCREEN, and the share is the unit.
  * Rehome the share list out of Local Library into Storage.
  * Each share is ONE ROW carrying its own state: track count, last scanned, and whether it is watching, scanning or errored. Actions (edit, remove) live on the row.
  * Library Management stops listing shares at all and becomes about the merged result — totals, duplicates, artwork coverage, cleanup.

DO NOT SPLIT 'ADD A SHARE' FROM 'SEE WHAT THAT SHARE CONTRIBUTED'. The instinct to have one screen for adding and another for reporting is the thing to resist. Roon does not do it, and the reason is that the share is the unit — its identity, its contents and its health are one subject.

NAMING — Storage over Share Management. The audience is audiophiles, many arriving from Roon where the term is already Storage, and it pairs naturally against Services. Share Management describes the mechanism; Storage describes the thing. Tom's own framing was 'share management or similar', so this is a recommendation rather than settled.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: a rename. Moving shares under a better heading without making the row carry its own state leaves the same tangle with new labels. If the row does not answer 'what is on this share and is it healthy' without a tap, the restructure has not happened.

OUT OF SCOPE — these need the Storage row to exist but are their own work, and folding them in is how a restructure becomes a redesign:
  * fAutoScanOnShareAdd — the scan starting automatically, and its progress/pause UI. The IA answer belongs here (progress lives ON THE SHARE ROW, beside track count and last-scanned, not on a screen the user must go find) but building it does not. That item already depends on this one.
  * fSourceAvailability — dimming content whose share is unreachable. Feeds the row; ships independently.
  * Whether fArtworkManagement and fArtworkManualSearchUtility are one screen or two. An artwork question, recorded on those items.

STILL DELIBERATELY DEFERRED past the UI work: fSonosEventSubscriptions and fHomeTheatreSettings. Interesting, non-blocking, and both would expand scope at exactly the wrong moment.

The four prerequisites this entry used to list — fZonePollingTestSeam, bGroupChangesMadeOutsideSorrivaAreNeverSeen, fArtworkHigherResolutionFetch and fArtworkProvenance — were all completed 2026-08-08. Nothing now gates this but the naming and scope decisions above, which are a conversation rather than a coding session.

CLOSED 2026-08-08 AS NO CHANGE NEEDED. Checking the screens against this entry showed it described what already exists.

Library Management holds library stats, a database-size card and Clear Library — no shares anywhere, which is already 'the merged result'. Local Library holds server cards, Network Share and Local Files, and a server opens its mapped shares. The share row ALREADY carries track count, last scanned or 'Never scanned', and scan state including 'Retrying skipped tracks…'. That was this entry's own test for whether the restructure had happened — if the row does not answer 'what is on this share and is it healthy' without a tap — and it passes.

THE RENAME IS ALSO WRONG, on evidence found while checking. Library Management already has a section labelled 'Storage' for the database-size card. Renaming Local Library to Storage would put two meanings of that word in one settings tree — 'where your music lives' and 'how much disk we use'. Worse than the current labels.

HOW THIS ENTRY CAME TO EXIST: it was written from a conversation about information architecture without looking at the screens first. The reasoning was sound and the conclusion was already implemented. Worth remembering before logging a structural feature — read the app, not the transcript.

What genuinely remains from that thread was always separate: fAutoScanOnShareAdd (scan progress on the share row) and fSourceAvailability (dim unreachable content). Neither needs a restructure first.

===================== RESCOPED 2026-08-20 =====================

This entry now covers HOME AND LOCK SCREEN WIDGETS ONLY. The lock-screen playback control Tom asked for is fLiveActivity, and the plumbing every surface shares is fAppIntents. Dynamic Island is a presentation of a Live Activity, not a separate build.

TWO THINGS DO NOT EXIST YET and are part of this entry: a widget extension target, and an APP GROUP. The App Group is not optional - a widget runs in its own process and cannot reach the GRDB database in the app container without one.

Buttons run through fAppIntents rather than being wired per-widget. Widget refresh budgets are stingy, so a home-screen widget is suited to STARTING something - a zone switcher, a library shortcut - rather than tracking live now-playing state, which is fLiveActivity's job.

Deployment target is iOS 26.5, so nothing here is version-gated.

HOME ONLY. Sorriva reaches speakers over the LAN; a widget is inert away from the network. Accepted - see fLiveActivity for why parity with Sonos is not available without a backend.

features.name: Scan failure review and targeted rescan utility
features.desc: Settings utility listing permanently failed scans with the specific failure reason for each file, plus a manual rescan action for a selected album. The manual rescan reads a larger block than the standard 64KB tag window. Scoped to a single album so the larger read does not create concurrent session pressure on the NAS. Addresses files whose VORBIS_COMMENT block falls outside the 64KB window because a large embedded PICTURE block precedes it in the FLAC metadata block order — these currently retry five times against identical bytes and fail permanently. RECLASSIFIED 2026-07-27: moved out of fScannerPolish/scanner hardening. The underlying limitation (large embedded PICTURE pushing VORBIS_COMMENT past the 64KB read window) is explicitly staying as a documented, accepted constraint at the parser level, not being fixed here — this is new product surface area (a Settings screen, a list view, a user-triggered rescan action) sitting on top of the scanner, not a correction to something the scanner gets wrong. Every other fScannerPolish item (bDuplicateAlbumDetection, bTagEditsNotDetected, bArtworkSelectionNotBestWins, bAlbumGenreFromFirstTrack) corrects scanner behavior directly; this one doesn't. Standalone feature, own priority/scheduling, not gated on or grouped with scanner work.

features.name: Post-scan reconciliation audit — files attempted vs processed vs DB records
features.desc:
2026-07-28. In-app audit, run after a scan completes, that reconciles two equations which must both balance: (1) files attempted = processed in main pass + resolved via retry + permanently failed; (2) DB record count = processed in main pass + resolved via retry (permanently-failed files correctly produce zero rows per bFailedReadCreatesWrongAlbumFromFallback, excluded by design not accident). Surfaces as a summary screen: Attempted / Processed / Resolved on Retry / Permanently Failed / DB Record Count, with a clear reconciled-or-discrepancy-of-N indicator. Intended location: Library Management (Tom's current lean, not fully decided) or Local Library. Pairs with fScanFailureUtility — this detects something's wrong, that lets the user act on the specific files once known. Also directly supports diagnosing bMissingTracksInAlbum, which is close to the exact tool its own investigation notes call for.

REQUIRES A SCOPING DECISION BEFORE BUILDING, not yet confirmed with Tom in detail: tracks don't currently carry a scan-session identifier, only createdAt/updatedAt timestamps. A time-window heuristic (rows touched between scan start/end) would work for most cases but leaves a real edge case ambiguous — a track updated by this scan that already existed from a prior one. Recommended: add an explicit scanSessionId to Track (and scan_skips), populated by the scanner on every write, so every row is unambiguously attributable to the run that touched it. This is a real, if small, schema addition — worth explicit sign-off before implementation, since the whole point of this feature is catching subtle counting bugs, and its own scoping needs to be unambiguous or a discrepancy becomes uncertain rather than diagnostic.

What already exists vs needs building: files-attempted count and main-pass skip/write-failure counts are already in the scan-start/scan-end log lines. Resolved-via-retry and permanently-failed totals are currently scattered across per-pass retry-scheduler log lines (PASS N COMPLETE), not aggregated into one final running tally — needs building. The DB count check itself is a simple query once the scanSessionId scoping question above is settled.

features.name: Subscribe to speaker events instead of polling (GENA)
features.desc:
Sorriva polls. Sonos can PUSH: UPnP GENA lets a controller subscribe to a speaker's AVTransport and RenderingControl and receive an HTTP callback whenever state changes. Sorriva has no subscriber today.

WHY IT IS FIRST. It is the prerequisite for a lock-screen widget that shows what is playing without being touched - the speaker is the only thing that knows, so either it tells us or we ask it, and asking requires us to be running.

IT PAYS FOR ITSELF WITHOUT THE WIDGET. It is how Sorriva would notice a change made in the Sonos app - shuffle turned off, a track skipped - without polling for it. It exposes the fields that are EVENT ONLY and therefore invisible to Sorriva today: r:EnqueuedTransportURI and its metadata, which is where a queue's origin survives and whose absence cost a full session on Spotify (sonos-playback-contract.md 12). And it takes load off a 2-second poll running against nine zones.

THE LISTENER PATTERN ALREADY EXISTS. SorrivaHTTPServer runs an NWListener HTTP server on port 8080 for AirPlay streaming. A GENA callback endpoint is the same shape.

EXIT QUESTION, AND IT IS THE POINT OF THE SPIKE: DOES A SUSPENDED APP STILL RECEIVE CALLBACKS? iOS suspends a process seconds after backgrounding and a suspended process is not servicing sockets. UNMEASURED - do not assume either way, and do not infer it from how the Sonos app behaves. Measure it on OUR app: subscribe, log every callback with a timestamp, background the app, lock the phone, change the track from another controller, and watch when they stop.

- Callbacks keep arriving -> a live lock-screen widget is straightforward, at home, with no cloud and no account.
- Callbacks stop at suspension -> fLiveActivity degrades to working controls with a last-known display, which is still shippable, and the alternative routes (a Network Extension app push provider, which needs an entitlement requested from Apple) get evaluated then rather than now.

Subscriptions expire and must be renewed on a timer; renewal failure must be visible rather than silently reverting to stale state.

features.name: App Intents - the shared foundation for every control surface
features.desc:
Play, pause, skip, volume, and 'play X in zone Y' expressed once as App Intents.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ITEM. Widget buttons, Live Activity buttons, Control Center controls, Siri, Shortcuts and the Action button ALL run through App Intents. Build them once and each surface is a thin presentation layer; build them per-surface and the same plumbing gets written three times and drifts.

An intent runs in the app's process and gets enough execution to complete a SOAP call to a speaker on the LAN - that is the path that makes a lock-screen button actually move a volume slider in the room.

Delivers value on its own before any widget exists: Siri and Shortcuts control, and the Action button.

Zone targeting is the design question - an intent needs to name a zone, and the zone list is dynamic. App Intents supports dynamic options for exactly this.

features.name: Live Activity and Dynamic Island for playback
features.desc:
FULL DESIGN ANALYSIS: engineering/live-activity-model.md - read it before building. It carries the ActivityKit model, the iOS suspension constraint that shapes everything, the fallback that ships without any of the hard parts, why Sonos's Control API is not a route, and the design decisions still open.

A lock-screen playback control for the zone you are listening to, with the Dynamic Island presentation.

DYNAMIC ISLAND IS NOT A SECOND FEATURE. It is one of the presentations of a Live Activity - compact, minimal, expanded. Build the activity and the Island comes with it.

WHAT IT SHOWS: what is playing, on which zone, with transport controls and volume. Controls run through fAppIntents.

HOME ONLY, BY ARCHITECTURE, AND THAT IS ACCEPTED. Sorriva reaches speakers over the LAN - no cloud, no account, no server. Off the network there is nothing to talk to. Tom, 2026-08-20: away-from-home playback 'would be nice but not a requirement or expectation'. The activity should END when the system is unreachable rather than sit there greyed with dead buttons - that is the behaviour observed on the Sonos widget and it is the right one. A stale control on a lock screen is worse than no control.

NO SONOS DEVELOPER ACCOUNT, API KEY, OR AGREEMENT IS REQUIRED FOR ANY OF THIS. The route is GENA (fSonosEventSubscriber) - the same undocumented UPnP interface Sorriva already uses for every other command. No registration, no OAuth, no user sign-in, no terms accepted. Anything below about Sonos's Control API is an ALTERNATIVE that was investigated and is NOT part of the plan.

WHY SONOS'S EQUIVALENT WORKS AWAY FROM HOME AND OURS WILL NOT: measured 2026-08-20 on Tom's phone - with wifi off, their widget kept working and the volume genuinely changed in the room, so it is cloud-relayed in both directions. Sorriva has no cloud by design and that is accepted.

----- INVESTIGATED, NOT ADOPTED: Sonos's Control API -----

CLOUD Control API: event subscription REQUIRES a registered public HTTPS callback URL that WE would have to host - it returns 403 without one. That is a backend, which Sorriva deliberately does not have. Commands away from home may be reachable through their cloud REST API without a backend; live state is not.

LOCAL Control API - A CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS ENTRY, which recorded it as unavailable by quoting Sonos's 'the Control API on the LAN is not available for wide release'. MEASURED 2026-08-20 against Listening Room: port 1443 is open and https://<ip>:1443/api/v1/players/local/info answers ERROR_API_KEY_VALIDATION_FAILED / 'Invalid api key'. A live endpoint asking for credentials, not an absent one - the same situation as the UPnP SOAP API Sorriva already depends on. Tom's point: unsupported has never meant unusable here.

IT REMAINS UNEVALUATED, DELIBERATELY. Finding out whether it beats GENA needs a developer API key, and obtaining one means registering and accepting Sonos's partner terms. Sorriva is a paid App Store app that competes with the Sonos app, built on an interface Sonos publishes for its own use; today there is no agreement with them at all, and signing one is a business decision rather than a technical step. The terms were not readable from the public docs. DO NOT register speculatively, and do not use a key extracted from Sonos's own app.

If that decision is ever taken, the two questions worth answering are whether the local API needs only a key or also OAuth against a Sonos account, and whether events can be delivered to a callback on the LAN rather than a hosted endpoint. Structured JSON instead of UPnP XML would be the payoff.

----- end of investigated-not-adopted -----

DEPENDS ON fSonosEventSubscriber for live display. If its spike shows callbacks stop at suspension, this degrades to working controls with a last-known display - still shippable, and a decision point rather than a blocker.
